schema.title: Response List Profiles Api Profiles Get

put.description:
Stars or unstars one profile. A factory preset takes a star too: the
star is the person's choice, and it leaves the preset's tuning alone.

get.description: Returns what the header shows. This never opens a link itself.

post.description:
Opens the link and runs the unit's startup sequence.

`LinkKeeper` connects by itself, so the frontend does not call this route.
This route reports a failure in the body, and not as an error status. An
unplugged unit is a normal state, and not a broken request.

get.description:
Reads what the unit is doing with sound, live from the unit.

Four reads in one action, so they share one lock and give one consistent
picture. Four separate reads could interleave with another caller.

This route stays out of `GET /api/device` on purpose. The header polls that
route, and it never opens a link. These reads cost USB exchanges.

post.description:
Sets the master volume, in dB.

The unit refuses a volume write with STATUS -6 while it holds THROUGH, and
takes one on an OTHER mode. Nobody measured CAR_SOURCE yet. So this route
writes first. Only a refusal makes it move the mode, write again, and put
the mode back. The refusal must not escape: `DeqDevice.run` drops the link
on any session error, and a refused volume is no broken link.
`scripts/probe_audio_output.py` does the same dance. A mode change cuts
the audio for a moment, so the route avoids one that the unit does not
need.

Tells the unit this device is ready to play audio (0x1a).

The real app sends it at the end of every cold start, and so does the
connect sequence here. Without it the car stayed silent for as long as the
Pi stayed attached. Sent alone in a car on 2026-10-11, it brought the audio
back at once. This endpoint stays as a lever for a link that is up but
silent. It has no body and the reply is a status only.

Picks which input the unit plays, and keeps it for the next links.

CAR_SOURCE plays the car's own audio through the DSP. THROUGH most likely
skips the DSP. The backend sets the stored mode on every new link.
Mutes or unmutes the unit, and answers with what it now holds.

get.description: Returns the value sets the unit accepts, read from the Pioneer app.

post.description: Sends one stored profile's DSP settings to the unit.

Reads the tune the unit holds now and stores it as a custom profile.

A unit that a Pioneer app tuned keeps that tune in its settings blob. This
route turns the blob into a profile, so a person keeps that tune before
a push replaces it.
Picks one of the unit's own EQ styles.
Picks one of the unit's own live-simulation modes.

get.description:
Returns the bridge's health, and everything that went wrong with it.

A read raises a notice when the health says so. That lets a power dip
outlive itself: the live reading recovers, and the notice stays until the
bridge restarts.
Returns the bridge's memory, disk, network, load and build.

Describes the web app that the bridge serves, for the car app's copy.

See `frontend_bundle.py`. A backend with no build answers 404.

Returns one part of the base64 zip. The reply names its build, so a
download that spans a release starts again.

put.description:
Makes one profile the active one, and pushes it when the unit is connected.

A second call with the same profile pushes it again. That is how the app
applies edits that came after the last push. A failed push answers 200 with
status failed: the choice still holds, and the next link tries again.

Picks the source mode for now and for every new link.

Unlike `POST /device/audio-source`, it answers 200 while the unit is not
connected. The choice then waits for the next link. The car app uses it
for that reason.

Picks the EQ that plays on top of the car profile, and pushes both.

`null` plays the car profile alone. A second call with the same EQ
pushes again, as with the profile.

schema.title: Response List Equalizers Api Equalizers Get

post.description: Copies any EQ, a factory one too, as a custom EQ to edit.

put.description:
Stars or unstars one EQ. A factory EQ takes a star too: the star is
the person's choice, and it leaves the curve alone.

Saves a new key. The Pi restarts a few seconds after this reply, so the
key applies and the phone loses the Pi for about a minute.

AccessPointKeyWrite.title: AccessPointKeyWrite
AccessPointKeyWrite.description:
A new key for the access point. It applies at the access point's
next start, which is the Pi's next boot.

AccessPointRead.title: AccessPointRead
AccessPointRead.description:
The Pi's own access point. It never carries the key: anyone in
Bluetooth range can read this.

ActiveEqualizerWrite.title: ActiveEqualizerWrite
ActiveEqualizerWrite.description: `None` plays the car profile with no EQ on top.

ActiveProfileRead.title: ActiveProfileRead
ActiveProfileRead.description:
What the unit should play, and whether it plays it now.

`profile_id` is the car profile and `equalizer_id` the EQ on top of it.
`status` is one of none, waiting, applied, outdated and failed, for the
two together. `problem` says why the last push failed. `source_mode` is
the mode that each new link gets.

ActiveSourceWrite.title: ActiveSourceWrite
ActiveSourceWrite.description: A name from the AUDIO_SOURCE enum.

AudioStateRead.title: AudioStateRead
AudioStateRead.description:
What the unit does with sound, read live from it.

A separate model from `DeviceRead`, on purpose. The header polls that one,
and it never opens a link. Every field here costs a request and a reply
over USB. So the caller chooses when to ask for them.

This model exists because a tuning can apply without error and still give
silence, and nothing said so before. On 2026-10-09 a person applied
profiles and EQ styles in a car with no sound at all. The app could not
show whether the unit was on mute, near the bottom of its volume range, or
on a source that plays nothing.

BridgeNoticeRead.title: BridgeNoticeRead
BridgeNoticeRead.description: One fault that the bridge saw since it started.

BridgeRead.title: BridgeRead
BridgeRead.description:
What the app shows about the machine that holds the link.

This model describes the bridge, and not the DEQ. The two fail for
different reasons and ask different things of a person. A DEQ that is off
is normal. A bridge that browns out has a fault in the wiring.

The undervoltage fields are `None` where the machine cannot tell. A laptop
has no `vcgencmd`, and `False` would be a claim it cannot make.

BridgeSystemRead.title: BridgeSystemRead
BridgeSystemRead.description:
The bridge's machine statistics, for the app's system dialog.

Each field is `None` where the machine cannot tell. A laptop has no Pi
model and no `vcgencmd`. `frontend_build` is the build id of the frontend
that the bridge serves now. The app compares it with its own build id, and
so tells a cached page from the current one.

DeqEnumValueRead.title: DeqEnumValueRead
DeqEnumValueRead.description: One value the unit accepts, as the Pioneer app declares it.

DeviceOptionsRead.title: DeviceOptionsRead
DeviceOptionsRead.description:
Every value set the unit's own DSP offers.

These come from the app, through `deq_enums.json`, so the frontend
never has to keep a list of its own.

DeviceRead.title: DeviceRead
DeviceRead.description: What the header shows about the unit.

EqStyleWrite.title: EqStyleWrite
EqStyleWrite.description: Which built-in EQ style to select on the unit.

FrontendBundleRead.title: FrontendBundleRead
FrontendBundleRead.description:
The web app that the bridge serves, as a base64 zip in parts.

`sha256` is the hash of the whole zip, after the parts are joined and
decoded.

LRBank.title: LRBank
LRBank.description:
A combined L+R graphic-EQ slot. `banks` holds one 13-value gain array
per storable bank (the device has multiple slots). `selectedBank` picks
which one is active. Frequencies follow the fixed 13-band table that
`expandEq` also gives explicitly per channel (50Hz-12.5kHz, doubling).

LibraryExport.title: LibraryExport
LibraryExport.description:
A person's own library, as one file: the custom profiles, the custom
EQs, and the stars on factory presets. The factory presets themselves
come with every install, so the file names them only by their name.

LibraryImportRead.title: LibraryImportRead
LibraryImportRead.description:
What an import added. An item that the library holds already, with
the same name and the same content, counts as skipped.

LibraryProfile.title: LibraryProfile
LibraryProfile.description:
A custom profile in an export. It has no id: the importing database
gives it a new one.

LiveSimulationWrite.title: LiveSimulationWrite
LiveSimulationWrite.description: Which built-in live-simulation mode to select on the unit.

NetworkInterfaceRead.title: NetworkInterfaceRead
NetworkInterfaceRead.description: One network interface of the bridge, without loopback.

TuningData.title: TuningData
TuningData.description:
Everything except `header`: the part that the EQ UI edits, and that the
backend writes to the device.

UnitProfileCreate.title: UnitProfileCreate
UnitProfileCreate.description: The name for a profile read from the unit.

UpdatesRead.title: UpdatesRead
UpdatesRead.description:
What the Pi's release updater last found.

`supported` is false on a machine with no updater, such as a laptop.
Then every other field keeps its default.

WifiNetworkWrite.title: WifiNetworkWrite
WifiNetworkWrite.description:
A network to save. An empty password saves an open network.

The helper on the bridge checks the same rules again. This check gives
the app a 422 before anything runs as root.

WifiRead.title: WifiRead
WifiRead.description:
The networks that the bridge joins, and the networks in range.

`visible` comes from the bridge's last scan. Nothing scans for this
request, because a scan touches the radio.
